title: E. coli Plating Quantification
author: Kenneth Schackart
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xqhfmt6

steps.title: Prepare 10⁶ serial dilution
steps.instruction: Create a series of six consecutive 10‑fold dilutions starting from the stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL of the stock solution to a 2 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 900 µL of DI water to the tube and mix to obtain a 1:10 dilution of the stock.
Using 100 µL of the resulting dilution, add it to a new tube containing 900 µL DI water; mix to obtain the second 1:10 dilution.
Repeat the previous transfer‑and‑add step a total of six times, so that the final solution is diluted by 10⁶ relative to the original stock.

steps.title: Plate chosen dilution
steps.instruction: Dispense and spread an appropriate diluted sample onto an agar plate.

substeps.instruction: Select the dilution you consider suitable for counting colonies.
Dispense 100 µL of the selected dilution onto the surface of an agar (agarose gel) plate.
Evenly spread the cell suspension over the agar using an inoculation loop, ensuring a uniform layer for colony counting.

steps.title: Seal and incubate plate
steps.instruction: Prepare the plated agar for incubation and label it.

substeps.instruction: Wrap the edge of the agar plate with Parafilm; if you have never used Parafilm, ask a TA for assistance.
Wait 2 minutes, then invert the plate (place it upside‑down) for incubation.
Label the plate with your group number, the date, and the dilution used (expressed as 10^x).

steps.title: Document incubated plate
steps.instruction: Capture an image of the grown colonies for reporting.

substeps.instruction: After incubation, take a clear image of the plate (performed by the TA).
Include this image in the results section of the lab report.

steps.title: Count colonies and calculate concentration
steps.instruction: Determine colony numbers and back‑calculate the original E. coli concentration.

substeps.instruction: Using the plate image, count the colonies either manually or with image‑processing software such as ImageJ.
Apply the provided equation to calculate the original E. coli concentration from the colony count and dilution factor.
Record the calculated concentration in the lab report.
